principles: Reuse proven experiment patterns (recovery-runner conventions) without coupling to product code
Every numeric constant in a selfcheck traces to a plan-reviewed anchor value
Immutability and gating by mechanical refusal, not documentation
Hash stability first: nothing time- or order-dependent enters a hashed payload
Hermetic selfchecks are the acceptance evidence and the red test
drivers: The plan's M0/M2/M5 exit criteria are already fixed and reviewed - implementation must satisfy them verbatim
The experiment dir must stay self-contained like recovery-runner (no imports from packages/*/src)
Operator chose single-host DEV + standard Lattice lifecycle (no dual-write)

options.name: self-contained-mjs-tools
pros: Mirrors the committed recovery-runner layout exactly (plain .mjs + selfchecks, no build step)
No coupling to packages/* so no product-code review floor
Formulas are small closed-form; local re-implementation with plan-anchored selfchecks is verifiable
cons: Small formula duplication vs analyze.mjs (mitigated by anchor-value selfchecks)

options.name: import-analyze-mjs-primitives
cons: Cross-directory coupling between two experiment suites; recovery-runner internals were not designed as a public API
Refactoring analyze.mjs later would silently affect ablation tools
Contradicts the self-containment convention both experiment dirs follow

options.name: typescript-in-packages-lab
pros: Type safety; shared with product tooling
cons: Turns an experiments-side story into a product-code story (build step, floor review, version bumps)
The plan S13 explicitly scopes these as experiment tooling reusing recovery-runner patterns

rationale: Matches the plan's S13 reuse framing (pattern reuse, not module import), keeps S1 out of product-code review floors, and the known risk (formula drift) is neutralized by selfcheck anchors that were triple-verified during the B-36fd review.

preMortem.scenario: Sample-size formula direction or variant drifts from the plan-reviewed numbers
preMortem.trigger: Implementing treatment = baseline + MDE, or an unpooled/continuity-corrected variant
preMortem.consequence: The M5 adequacy report mis-sizes M7 and contradicts the decision doc; a future powered run is over- or under-sized
preMortem.mitigation: Selfcheck asserts the four anchor values (294/62/27/58) and the in-band maximum location; any variant change breaks the selfcheck; the direction is stated in a comment and in the report output

preMortem.scenario: Protocol hash is unstable across key order or environments
preMortem.trigger: Hashing JSON.stringify of an object with nondeterministic key order, or including createdAt/timestamps in the payload
preMortem.consequence: Same protocol produces different hashes; ledger/protocol binding breaks; false tamper alarms
preMortem.mitigation: Canonical serialization (sorted keys, hash field excluded, timestamps outside the hashed payload); selfcheck asserts hash stability across key reordering and hash change on any field tamper

preMortem.scenario: Immutability refusal has a race or bypass
preMortem.trigger: build checks score-records.jsonl then writes non-atomically, or a mutating path forgets the check
preMortem.consequence: A ledger silently changes after outcomes exist - the exact pre-registration violation the plan forbids
preMortem.mitigation: Single guard function called by every mutating entry point; write-temp-then-rename; selfcheck covers refusal-after-score-record and verify-detects-tamper

preMortem.scenario: Selfchecks depend on repo state and rot when unrelated files move
preMortem.trigger: Selfcheck reading recovery-runner files or the real .lattice store
preMortem.consequence: S1 selfchecks fail on unrelated repo changes; flaky gate evidence
preMortem.mitigation: Hermetic temp-dir experiment roots only; no reads outside the new directory and its temp roots
